question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding Fundamental Rights?
option_1: Fundamental Rights can be enforced by Law.
option_2: Fundamental rights are derived from the Britain Constitution.
option_3: The Fundamental Rights are mentioned in constitution from article 12 to 35.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fundamental rights are derived from the Britain Constitution.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Fundamental Rights enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution were mainly borrowed/derived from the Constitution of the United States of America (Bill of Rights), not Britain. (मौलिक अधिकार — अमेरिकी संविधान से प्रेरित)

 

• The British Constitution, being unwritten and based on parliamentary sovereignty, does not have a codified 'Bill of Rights' comparable to India's Fundamental Rights; India instead borrowed concepts like the rule of law, parliamentary system and single citizenship from Britain — not fundamental rights.

 

• Since the statement wrongly attributes the source of Fundamental Rights to Britain, it is the INCORRECT statement and hence the correct answer to this question.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Duties (added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976) were inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR (Russia).

 

• The Directive Principles of State Policy were borrowed from the Irish Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Correct statement — Fundamental Rights are justiciable and can be enforced through courts of law, primarily via Article 32.

 

• Option 3: Correct statement — Fundamental Rights are contained in Part III, covering Articles 12 to 35 of the Constitution.

 

• Option 4: Correct statement — Article 21 guarantees the Right to Life and Personal Liberty.

question: Under which scheme are collateral free loans of up to ₹10 Lakh extended by the Member Lending Institutions (MLIs) in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) was launched on 8 April 2015 to provide collateral-free loans of up to ₹10 lakh to non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises. (प्रधानमंत्री मुद्रा योजना — असुरक्षित ऋण योजना)

 

• Loans under PMMY are extended by Member Lending Institutions (MLIs) — Banks, NBFCs and MFIs — and are called MUDRA (Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency) loans.

 

• The loans are categorised into three products — Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishor (₹50,000 to ₹5 lakh) and Tarun (₹5 lakh to ₹10 lakh) — signifying the stage of growth of the beneficiary business unit.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• MUDRA Ltd. is a subsidiary set up by SIDBI (Small Industries Development Bank of India).

 

• A new category, Tarun Plus, was later added for loans between ₹10 lakh and ₹20 lakh for those who have availed and successfully repaid the earlier 'Tarun' category loan.

 

NOTE

 

• National Strategy for Financial Inclusion (Option 1): A strategy document by RBI (2019-2024) for broadening access to financial services, not a specific loan scheme.

 

• Stand Up India scheme (Option 3): Facilitates bank loans between ₹10 lakh and ₹1 crore to at least one SC/ST and one woman borrower per bank branch for setting up greenfield enterprises — a different loan range from MUDRA.

 

• Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (Option 4): A financial inclusion scheme for universal access to banking (savings/current accounts), not a collateral-free business loan scheme.

question: Which of the following festivals observed in Assam is majorly celebrated by Vaishnavites?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Doljatra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Doljatra (Dol Jatra), the Assamese equivalent of Holi, is majorly celebrated by Vaishnavites at the Sattras (Vaishnavite monasteries) founded by the saint-reformer Srimanta Sankardev. (डोल जात्रा — वैष्णव त्योहार, असम)

 

• It is celebrated with great fervour at Sattras such as Barpeta Sattra and Auniati Sattra, involving devotional singing (Naam-Kirtan), colour-play and worship of Lord Krishna.

 

• It generally coincides with Holi/Phagwah, celebrated in the Assamese month of Phagun (February-March).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bihu is the principal secular/agricultural festival of Assam, celebrated by all communities (Bohag/Rongali, Kati/Kongali, and Magh/Bhogali Bihu), not specifically a Vaishnavite festival.

 

• The Sattra institution of Assam, founded by Srimanta Sankardev in the 15th-16th century, is the nerve centre of Neo-Vaishnavism (Ek Sarana Naam Dharma) in the state.

 

NOTE

 

• Bihu (Option 1): A pan-Assamese seasonal/agricultural festival, not tied specifically to Vaishnavism.

 

• Ambuchi Mela (Option 3): Associated with Kamakhya Temple, linked to Shakti/Tantric worship, not Vaishnavism.

 

• Rongker (Option 4): A community festival of the Karbi tribal community involving animistic worship, unrelated to Vaishnavism.

question: Which of the following group of months is the coldest in North India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is December and January.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In North India, the cold weather (winter) season spans roughly from mid-November to February, with December and January being the coldest months. (शीत ऋतु — दिसंबर व जनवरी सबसे ठंडे महीने)

 

• During this period, north-easterly/north-westerly winds blow from the interior of the continent (high pressure over the Indian landmass) towards the sea, bringing dry and cold conditions, particularly severe in the northern plains due to their distance from the moderating influence of the sea.

 

• Occasional Western Disturbances originating over the Mediterranean Sea bring light winter rainfall to North India during these months, which is crucial for the rabi crop.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's climatic seasons (as per the India Meteorological Department) are broadly classified into four: Winter (December-February), Summer/Pre-monsoon (March-May), South-West Monsoon (June-September), and Post-monsoon/Retreating monsoon (October-November).

 

• May is generally the hottest month in most parts of North India before the onset of the monsoon.

 

NOTE

 

• February and March (Option 1): This period marks the transition from winter to summer, not the coldest.

 

• September and October (Option 2): This falls in the retreating/post-monsoon season, still relatively warm and humid.

 

• October and November (Option 4): This is the post-monsoon (retreating monsoon) period, cooler than the preceding months but not as cold as December-January.

question: Some of the talas invented by ____________ include Trimukhi, Panchamukhi, Saptamukhi and Navamukhi.
solution_text:
The correct answer is M Balamuralikrishna.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mangalampalli Balamuralikrishna, the eminent Carnatic vocalist, composer and multi-instrumentalist, is credited with inventing several new talas (rhythmic cycles), including Trimukhi, Panchamukhi, Saptamukhi and Navamukhi. (एम. बालमुरलीकृष्ण — नई तालों के रचयिता)

 

• He also created new ragas such as Lavangi, Mahati, Sumukham, Sarvashri and Trisakthi, and composed thillanas in multiple languages, showcasing his versatility beyond traditional Carnatic forms.

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan (1991) and the Bharat Ratna nomination discourse aside, he remains one of the most decorated Carnatic musicians, also a recipient of the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Balamuralikrishna was a child prodigy who gave his first public performance at the age of eight and started composing at the age of fourteen.

 

• He also acted in and composed music for several films, including the National Award-winning score for the Kannada film Hamsageethe (1975).

 

NOTE

 

• Hariprasad Chaurasia (Option 2): A renowned Hindustani classical flute (bansuri) maestro, not associated with inventing these talas.

 

• Yashraj (Option 3): Not a classical musician associated with tala innovation in this context.

 

• Bhimsen Joshi (Option 4): A legendary Hindustani classical vocalist of the Kirana Gharana, unrelated to these Carnatic talas.

question: In which year was the temple entry movement started by Bhimrao Ambedkar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1927.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dr. B. R. Ambedkar launched the temple entry movement in 1927, beginning with the Mahad Satyagraha (March 1927) to assert the right of the depressed classes to draw water from the Chavadar Tank at Mahad, Maharashtra, followed by efforts for temple entry. (मंदिर प्रवेश आंदोलन — 1927, भीमराव अंबेडकर)

 

• This was followed by the more direct Kalaram Temple Satyagraha at Nashik (starting 1930), where Ambedkar led thousands of Dalits demanding entry into the Kalaram Temple.

 

• The movement aimed to challenge the practice of untouchability and secure equal religious and social rights for the depressed classes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Mahad Satyagraha is also remembered for the public burning of the Manusmriti by Ambedkar on 25 December 1927, symbolising rejection of the caste-based social order.

 

• Ambedkar later famously stated he was 'born a Hindu but would not die a Hindu,' reflecting his eventual conversion to Buddhism in 1956.

 

NOTE

 

• 1935 (Option 1): This year is associated with the Government of India Act, 1935, not the start of the temple entry movement.

 

• 1918 (Option 2): Too early; Ambedkar had just returned from higher studies abroad around this period and had not yet launched this movement.

 

• 1922 (Option 4): Not the correct year for the launch of the temple entry movement.

question: Who among the following dancers was the first one from the state of Odisha to be conferred the Padma Vibhushan Award?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kelucharan Mohapatra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kelucharan Mohapatra, the legendary Odissi dance guru, was the first dancer from Odisha to be conferred the Padma Vibhushan, awarded in the year 2000. (केलुचरण महापात्र — ओडिशा से प्रथम पद्म विभूषण नर्तक)

 

• He is widely regarded as one of the chief architects of the revival of Odissi dance as a classical dance form in independent India, along with figures like Pankaj Charan Das and Debaprasad Das.

 

• He trained several celebrated Odissi dancers, including Sonal Mansingh, Sanjukta Panigrahi and Madhavi Mudgal, and was also a skilled Pakhawaj player and Gotipua/Chhau performer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kelucharan Mohapatra was earlier honoured with the Padma Shri (1972) and Padma Bhushan (1988) before receiving the Padma Vibhushan in 2000, the same year he passed away.

 

• The Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra Odissi Research Centre in Bhubaneswar is named in his honour.

 

NOTE

 

• Uday Shankar (Option 1): A pioneer of modern Indian dance and creative dance, hailing from Bengal/Uttar Pradesh region, not Odisha.

 

• Pandit Birju Maharaj (Option 2): A doyen of Kathak dance from the Lucknow Gharana, belonging to Uttar Pradesh, not Odisha.

 

• Guru Bipin Singh (Option 4): A renowned exponent and reviver of Manipuri dance, belonging to Manipur, not Odisha.

question: Sankalp Gupta is associated with which of the following events?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chess.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sankalp Gupta is an Indian chess Grandmaster (GM), known for his strong performances in international chess events. (संकल्प गुप्ता — शतरंज ग्रैंडमास्टर)

 

• He earned his Grandmaster title through consistent strong results and norms in various international tournaments, becoming one of India's growing pool of young chess Grandmasters.

 

• India has seen a rapid rise in the number of chess Grandmasters in recent years, with players like Sankalp Gupta contributing to the country's strength in the sport.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's chess growth has been spearheaded by legends like Viswanathan Anand, and more recently by young stars such as D. Gukesh, R. Praggnanandhaa and Arjun Erigaisi.

 

• D. Gukesh became the World Chess Champion in 2024, defeating Ding Liren, becoming the youngest ever undisputed World Champion.

 

NOTE

 

• Wrestling (Option 2): Sankalp Gupta is not associated with wrestling; notable Indian wrestlers include Bajrang Punia and Vinesh Phogat.

 

• Badminton (Option 3): Sankalp Gupta is not a badminton player; this sport is associated with players like PV Sindhu and Lakshya Sen.

 

• Boxing (Option 4): Sankalp Gupta is not a boxer; Indian boxing is associated with athletes like Nikhat Zareen and Mary Kom.

question: Where was the 1912 session of the India National Congress held in Bihar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bankipore.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 1912 session of the Indian National Congress, its 27th session, was held at Bankipore (Patna), Bihar, and was presided over by Raghunath Narasinha Mudholkar. (बांकीपुर अधिवेशन 1912 — भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस)

 

• This was the first INC session held in Bihar, marking an important milestone in extending the Congress's reach into the region.

 

• Notable Bihar leader Mazharul Haque delivered a significant welcome address at this session, and the event helped galvanise nationalist sentiment in the region, later contributing to Bihar's separation from the Bengal Presidency in 1912.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The year 1912 also saw the creation of Bihar and Orissa as a separate province from the Bengal Presidency.

 

• A later INC session was also held in Gaya (1922), presided over by Chittaranjan Das, which is often confused with the Bankipore session.

 

NOTE

 

• Sahasaram (Option 1): No INC session of this scale was held here; historically notable for Sher Shah Suri's tomb.

 

• Gaya (Option 2): Venue of the 1922 INC session (Chittaranjan Das presiding), not the 1912 session.

 

• Madhubani (Option 4): Known for its folk art tradition, not a venue for the 1912 INC session.

question: Harmonium player, Tulsidas Borkar, was awarded with the ___________ in 2016.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Padma Shri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Tulsidas Borkar, an acclaimed harmonium exponent known for popularising the harmonium as a solo classical instrument, was awarded the Padma Shri in 2016. (तुलसीदास बोरकर — पद्म श्री, 2016)

 

• He trained under stalwarts including Pandit Ram Marathe and was a disciple in the Gwalior-Jaipur gharana tradition, celebrated for his solo harmonium recitals.

 

• He passed away in 2021, and is remembered as one of the foremost harmonium maestros of India, having accompanied numerous legendary vocalists over his career.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Padma Awards are India's civilian honours, given in three categories in ascending order: Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Vibhushan, with Bharat Ratna being the highest civilian award of the country.

 

• Padma Awards are announced annually on the eve of Republic Day (26 January).

 

NOTE

 

• Padma Bhushan (Option 2): A higher-tier civilian award; Tulsidas Borkar received the Padma Shri, not the Padma Bhushan.

 

• Bharat Ratna (Option 3): India's highest civilian award, not conferred on Tulsidas Borkar.

 

• Padma Vibhushan (Option 4): The second-highest civilian award; not the one conferred on him in 2016.

question: Which ocean is encircling the continent of Antarctica and extends northward to 60 degrees south latitude?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Southern Ocean.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Southern Ocean (also called the Antarctic Ocean) encircles the continent of Antarctica and is generally defined as extending from the Antarctic coast northward to 60°S latitude. (दक्षिणी महासागर — अंटार्कटिका के चारों ओर)

 

• It is the fourth-largest of the world's five oceans (after the Pacific, Atlantic and Indian, and larger than the Arctic), officially recognised as a distinct ocean by the International Hydrographic Organization in 2000.

 

• The Southern Ocean is characterised by the Antarctic Circumpolar Current (ACC), the strongest ocean current in the world, which flows uninterrupted around Antarctica.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Southern Ocean's boundary at 60°S latitude was adopted to coincide with the Antarctic Treaty System boundary.

 

• The Southern Ocean is important for global climate regulation, hosting significant marine biodiversity such as krill, whales and penguins.

 

NOTE

 

• Atlantic Ocean (Option 1): Lies between the Americas and Europe/Africa, bordering but not defined as encircling Antarctica.

 

• Indian Ocean (Option 2): Lies between Africa, Asia and Australia; bordered by, but does not itself encircle, Antarctica.

 

• Pacific Ocean (Option 3): The largest ocean, bordering Antarctica on one side, but does not encircle the entire continent.

question: Which Article mentions the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 148.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 148 of the Indian Constitution provides for the establishment of the office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG). (नियंत्रक एवं महालेखा परीक्षक — अनुच्छेद 148)

 

• The CAG is appointed by the President of India and holds office for a term of six years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier, and can only be removed in the manner similar to a Supreme Court judge.

 

• The CAG audits the accounts of the Union and State Governments and submits reports relating to the accounts of the Union to the President, who causes them to be laid before Parliament (Articles 149-151).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The CAG is often described as the 'Guardian of the Public Purse' and is a key pillar of financial accountability in India's constitutional framework.

 

• Articles 148 to 151 deal with the CAG — Article 148 (appointment and conditions of service), Article 149 (duties and powers), Article 150 (form of accounts) and Article 151 (audit reports).

 

NOTE

 

• Article 154 (Option 1): Deals with the executive power of the State, vested in the Governor.

 

• Article 156 (Option 2): Deals with the term of office of the Governor of a State.

 

• Article 136 (Option 4): Grants the Supreme Court special power to grant special leave to appeal.

question: Who among the following is the first Indian to win gold at Junior World Weightlifting Championship in May 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Harshada Sharad Garud.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Harshada Sharad Garud became the first Indian weightlifter to win a gold medal at the IWF Junior World Weightlifting Championship, achieving this feat in May 2022 in the 45 kg category held in Heraklion, Greece. (हर्षदा शरद गरुड़ — जूनियर विश्व भारोत्तोलन में भारत का प्रथम स्वर्ण)

 

• She set new junior world records in the process, lifting a combined total that surpassed the existing marks, cementing her achievement as historic for Indian weightlifting.

 

• Her victory was celebrated as a landmark moment for Indian weightlifting at the junior/youth level, inspiring the next generation of lifters.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mirabai Chanu is a senior Indian weightlifter and Olympic medallist (Silver, Tokyo 2020, 49 kg category), but she is not the athlete associated with this Junior World Championship gold.

 

• India's weightlifting programme has produced multiple international medallists, including Sathish Sivalingam, a multiple-time Commonwealth Games gold medallist.

 

NOTE

 

• Sathish Sivalingam (Option 1): A senior Indian weightlifter, known for Commonwealth Games golds, not this junior world title.

 

• Mirabai Chanu (Option 2): An Olympic and World Championship medallist at the senior level, not the first Indian to win junior world gold.

 

• Santoshi Matsa (Option 3): Not the weightlifter associated with this specific first-ever junior world gold for India.

question: The real name of Babur, the founder of Mughal dynasty in India was:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Zahiruddin Muhammad.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Babur, the founder of the Mughal dynasty in India, was born Zahir-ud-din Muhammad; 'Babur' (meaning 'tiger' in Chagatai/Turkic) was a title/nickname by which he became popularly known. (ज़हीरुद्दीन मुहम्मद बाबर — मुगल वंश के संस्थापक)

 

• Babur established Mughal rule in India after defeating Ibrahim Lodi, the last Sultan of the Lodi dynasty, in the First Battle of Panipat, 1526.

 

• He was a descendant of Timur on his father's side and Genghis Khan on his mother's side, and hailed from the Fergana Valley (present-day Uzbekistan).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Babur authored the Baburnama (Tuzuk-i-Baburi), his memoirs written in the Chagatai Turkic language, considered an important historical and literary source.

 

• Babur also won the Battle of Khanwa (1527) against Rana Sanga of Mewar and the Battle of Ghaghra (1529) against the Afghans, consolidating Mughal power in North India.

 

NOTE

 

• Irfanuddin Muhammad (Option 2): Not Babur's actual name; a distractor option.

 

• Zainuddin Muhammad (Option 3): Not Babur's actual name; a distractor option.

 

• Ruknuddin Muhammad (Option 4): Not Babur's actual name; a distractor option.

question: About what percentage of passenger traffic is carried by roads in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 87%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Roads carry about 87% of the country's passenger traffic, making road transport the dominant mode for passenger movement in India. (सड़क परिवहन — लगभग 87% यात्री यातायात)

 

• India has one of the largest road networks in the world, spanning over 63 lakh km, comprising National Highways, State Highways, and district/rural roads.

 

• The dominance of roads is attributed to their flexibility, door-to-door connectivity, and reach into rural and remote areas not served by rail.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Roads also carry roughly 60-65% of India's freight traffic, alongside their dominant share of passenger movement.

 

• The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) and agencies like the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) are responsible for the development of India's road infrastructure.

 

NOTE

 

• 77% (Option 1): Understates the actual figure of road-based passenger traffic share.

 

• 57% (Option 3): Understates the actual figure of road-based passenger traffic share.

 

• 67% (Option 4): Understates the actual figure of road-based passenger traffic share.

question: Rudrankksh Patil is associated with _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is shooting.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rudrankksh Balasaheb Patil is an Indian sport shooter who specialises in the 10m Air Rifle event. (रुद्रांक्ष पाटिल — निशानेबाजी)

 

• He won a gold medal at the 2022 ISSF World Championship held in Cairo, Egypt, in the Men's 10m Air Rifle event, also setting a world record score in the process.

 

• He became one of the youngest Indian shooters to achieve a World Championship gold, boosting his profile as a strong prospect for future Olympic campaigns.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other prominent Indian air rifle/pistol shooters include Abhinav Bindra (India's first individual Olympic gold medallist, 2008 Beijing) and Manu Bhaker, who won bronze medals in shooting at the 2024 Paris Olympics.

 

• The National Rifle Association of India (NRAI) is the governing body for shooting sports in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Badminton (Option 1): Rudrankksh Patil is not a badminton player; that sport is associated with players like PV Sindhu.

 

• Chess (Option 3): Rudrankksh Patil is not a chess player.

 

• Wrestling (Option 4): Rudrankksh Patil is not a wrestler; Indian wrestling is associated with athletes like Bajrang Punia.

question: Which of the following classes includes the family of turtles?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Reptilia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Turtles belong to the class Reptilia, specifically the order Testudines (Chelonia), which includes turtles, tortoises and terrapins. (कछुआ — सरीसृप वर्ग, Reptilia)

 

• Reptiles are characterised by dry, scaly skin, being ectothermic (cold-blooded), and typically laying amniotic eggs with a leathery or hard shell on land.

 

• Turtles are unique among reptiles for possessing a bony or cartilaginous shell developed from their ribs, which serves as a shield against predators.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known members of class Reptilia include snakes, lizards, crocodiles and alligators.

 

• India's Wildlife Protection Act, 1972 provides protection to several turtle and tortoise species, such as the Olive Ridley turtle, which nests on the Odisha coast.

 

NOTE

 

• Chondrichthyes (Option 1): The class of cartilaginous fishes, such as sharks and rays, not turtles.

 

• Amphibia (Option 3): The class comprising frogs, toads and salamanders, which live a dual aquatic-terrestrial life; turtles are not amphibians.

 

• Aves (Option 4): The class of birds, unrelated to turtles.

question: According to the Census of India 2001, which of the following is the main reason that Indian men migrate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Work and employment.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to the Census of India 2001, the primary reason for migration among men in India is 'work and employment', reflecting the search for better economic opportunities. (जनगणना 2001 — पुरुष प्रवासन का मुख्य कारण: रोजगार)

 

• In contrast, for women, the predominant reason for migration recorded by the Census is 'marriage', since women in India commonly relocate to their husband's place after marriage.

 

• Migration data from Census 2001 (and later Census 2011) reveals a clear gendered pattern of migration reasons in India, useful for policy planning around labour and urbanisation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Census-recorded reasons for migration include 'moved after birth', 'moved with household', 'education' and 'business', but these rank lower than work/employment for men and marriage for women.

 

• Migration streams are classified in the Census as rural-to-rural, rural-to-urban, urban-to-rural, and urban-to-urban, with rural-to-urban migration often dominated by employment-seeking men.

 

NOTE

 

• Education (Option 1): A recorded reason for migration but not the predominant one for men.

 

• Marriage (Option 2): The main reason for migration among women, not men, as per Census 2001.

 

• Business (Option 4): A minor recorded reason for migration, not the predominant one for men.

question: Which of the following States have enacted the Cattle Preservation Act, 2021 in July-August 2021 to regulate slaughter and transport of cattle and proposed an amendment in December 2021 to allow inter-district transportation of cattle for agricultural and animal husbandry except in districts sharing international border?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Assam Cattle Preservation Act, 2021 was enacted by the Government of Assam in August 2021, regulating the slaughter, consumption and transport of cattle across the state. (असम मवेशी संरक्षण अधिनियम, 2021 — असम)

 

• In December 2021, an amendment was proposed to allow inter-district transportation of cattle for agricultural and animal husbandry purposes, except in districts sharing an international border, to prevent cross-border cattle smuggling.

 

• The Act replaced the earlier Assam Cattle Preservation Act, 1950, and imposed stricter conditions, including banning cattle slaughter near temples, satras, and other religious places, and within a 5 km radius of such institutions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Act was piloted by Assam's Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, aimed at curbing illegal cattle smuggling, especially across the India-Bangladesh border.

 

• Similar cattle protection/preservation laws exist in various forms across several Indian states, though the specific 2021 Act with this December 2021 amendment provision pertains to Assam.

 

NOTE

 

• Tripura (Option 1): Has not enacted this specific Cattle Preservation Act, 2021 with the described provisions.

 

• Sikkim (Option 2): Has not enacted this specific Cattle Preservation Act, 2021 with the described provisions.

 

• Arunachal Pradesh (Option 3): Has not enacted this specific Cattle Preservation Act, 2021 with the described provisions.

question: Which types of gametes are found in Spirogyra?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Isogamous and non-flagellated.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Spirogyra, a filamentous green alga, reproduces sexually through conjugation, involving the fusion of two similar (isogamous), non-motile (non-flagellated) gametes called aplanogametes. (स्पाइरोगायरा — समयुग्मक, अकशाभिक युग्मक)

 

• Since the gametes are morphologically and physiologically identical (isogamous) and lack flagella (non-flagellated), fusion occurs via formation of a conjugation tube, through which the cytoplasmic contents of one cell (acting as male) migrate into another (acting as female) to form a zygospore.

 

• This mode of reproduction is characteristic of many members of the class Chlorophyceae (green algae), and distinguishes Spirogyra from algae with motile gametes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The resulting zygospore formed after conjugation in Spirogyra has a thick protective wall and can remain dormant through unfavourable conditions before germinating.

 

• Spirogyra is commonly found in fresh water, stagnant ponds and is popularly called 'pond silk' or 'water silk' due to its slimy, thread-like filamentous appearance.

 

NOTE

 

• Isogamous and flagellated (Option 1): Incorrect; while the gametes are isogamous, they are non-flagellated (non-motile), not flagellated.

 

• Heterogamous and non-flagellated (Option 2): Incorrect; Spirogyra gametes are isogamous (similar), not heterogamous (dissimilar).

 

• Heterogamous and flagellated (Option 3): Incorrect on both counts; Spirogyra gametes are isogamous and non-flagellated.

question: The 'Make in India' initiative primarily focuses on which sector?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manufacturing.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 'Make in India' initiative was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 25 September 2014 to transform India into a global design and manufacturing hub. (मेक इन इंडिया — विनिर्माण क्षेत्र को बढ़ावा)

 

• Its primary objectives include increasing the manufacturing sector's contribution to GDP to 25%, creating millions of jobs, and improving India's ease of doing business ranking to attract Foreign Direct Investment (FDI).

 

• The initiative initially focused on 25 sectors, including automobiles, aviation, chemicals, defence manufacturing, electronics, pharmaceuticals, textiles and more, all falling under the broad manufacturing umbrella.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• 'Make in India' is administered by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

 

• Related initiatives complementing 'Make in India' include the Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, Startup India, and Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan.

 

NOTE

 

• Service (Option 2): While India's services sector is significant, it is not the primary focus of the Make in India initiative.

 

• Agriculture (Option 3): Not the primary focus sector of this initiative; agriculture is addressed by separate schemes.

 

• Import (Option 4): The initiative actually seeks to reduce import dependence and boost domestic manufacturing/exports, not promote imports.

question: Which of the following was NOT one of the basic attributes of Ashokas' Dhamma?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Celibacy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Emperor Ashoka's Dhamma was a set of ethical and social principles, not a religious doctrine, and its basic attributes included ahimsa (non-violence), tolerance/secularism, and social harmony/political unification — but not celibacy. (अशोक का धम्म — अहिंसा, सहिष्णुता; ब्रह्मचर्य इसमें शामिल नहीं)

 

• Dhamma emphasised values such as respect for elders, kindness to servants and slaves, generosity towards Brahmins and Sramanas, and non-injury to living beings, aiming at general moral welfare rather than monastic renunciation.

 

• Celibacy (Brahmacharya) is a monastic vow specific to renunciate orders (like Buddhist monks) but was not propagated by Ashoka as a component of Dhamma meant for the general populace.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ashoka propagated Dhamma through rock edicts and pillar edicts, inscribed in Prakrit (using Brahmi and Kharoshthi scripts), and appointed special officers called Dhamma Mahamatras to spread these values.

 

• Ashoka's Dhamma is often distinguished from Buddhism itself — it was a broader ethical code intended to unite his vast, diverse empire rather than a call to formal conversion.

 

NOTE

 

• Political unification (Option 1): A recognised attribute/goal of Dhamma, aimed at fostering unity across Ashoka's vast empire.

 

• Ahimsa (Option 2): A core and well-documented attribute of Ashoka's Dhamma, emphasising non-violence towards humans and animals.

 

• Secularism (Option 4): Ashoka's Dhamma promoted religious tolerance among all sects, reflecting a secular approach to governance.

question: N. Rangasamy sworn in as the Chief Minister of Puducherry in May 2021. What is the name of the party he formed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is All India NR Congress.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• N. Rangasamy was sworn in as the Chief Minister of Puducherry in May 2021, leading the party he founded, the All India N.R. Congress (AINRC). (एन. रंगासामी — ऑल इंडिया एनआर कांग्रेस, पुडुचेरी)

 

• The AINRC was founded by N. Rangasamy in 2011 after he broke away from the Indian National Congress, and it went on to form the government in Puducherry in alliance with the BJP in the 2021 Assembly elections.

 

• This marked Rangasamy's fourth term as Chief Minister of Puducherry, having previously served in this role multiple times since 2001.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Puducherry is a Union Territory with a legislature, and its Chief Minister heads the elected government alongside a Lieutenant Governor appointed by the Centre.

 

• The AINRC's symbol is the 'hut', and the party has largely remained a Puducherry-centric regional political outfit.

 

NOTE

 

• Naam Tamilar Katchi (Option 1): A Tamil Nadu-based regional party founded by Seeman, unrelated to N. Rangasamy.

 

• Amma Makkal Munnettra Kazagam (Option 3): A Tamil Nadu political party founded by T. T. V. Dhinakaran, unrelated to N. Rangasamy.

 

• Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (Option 4): A Tamil Nadu political party led by Thol. Thirumavalavan, unrelated to N. Rangasamy.

question: Identify the INCORRECT pair regarding motion and their examples?
option_1: Translatory motion – A ball falling from the cliff
option_2: Periodic motion – Hands of a clock
option_3: Oscillatory motion – Earth moving around the sun
option_4: Rotatory motion – blades of a fan
solution_text:
The correct answer is Oscillatory motion – Earth moving around the sun.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Earth moving around the Sun is an example of periodic (orbital/revolutionary) motion, not oscillatory motion, making this the INCORRECT pair. (दोलन गति नहीं, आवर्ती/परिक्रमण गति — पृथ्वी की सूर्य परिक्रमा)

 

• Oscillatory motion refers to a to-and-fro movement about a fixed mean position, such as that of a simple pendulum or a spring-mass system, which is distinct from the Earth's continuous, one-directional orbital path around the Sun.

 

• While the Earth's revolution around the Sun is periodic (it repeats after a fixed interval, one year), it is not oscillatory, since the Earth does not move back and forth about a mean position — it consistently sweeps through a closed, roughly elliptical orbit.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• All oscillatory motions are periodic, but not all periodic motions are oscillatory (e.g., uniform circular motion and orbital motion are periodic but not oscillatory).

 

• Examples of true oscillatory motion include the vibration of a guitar string, a swinging pendulum, and a mass attached to a spring.

 

NOTE

 

• Translatory motion – A ball falling from the cliff (Option 1): Correct pairing; a freely falling ball moves in a straight line without rotation, an example of rectilinear translatory motion.

 

• Periodic motion – Hands of a clock (Option 2): Correct pairing; the hands of a clock repeat their motion at fixed, regular intervals, a classic example of periodic motion.

 

• Rotatory motion – blades of a fan (Option 4): Correct pairing; fan blades spin about a fixed axis, a standard example of rotatory motion.

question: Which gas is evolved when iron and water react?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hydrogen.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When iron reacts with water (in the form of steam), it produces iron oxide (Fe₃O₄) and releases hydrogen gas (H₂). (लोहा और भाप की अभिक्रिया — हाइड्रोजन गैस उत्पन्न)

 

• The reaction is represented as: 3Fe + 4H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + 4H₂, typically occurring when iron is exposed to steam at high temperature.

 

• This reaction is a classic example of a metal-water (metal-steam) reaction, illustrating the reactivity series position of iron, which reacts with steam but not readily with cold water (unlike more reactive metals such as sodium or potassium).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Highly reactive metals like sodium and potassium react vigorously even with cold water, releasing hydrogen gas and often catching fire due to the heat generated.

 

• Metals like calcium and magnesium react with water at moderate rates, while metals like gold and silver do not react with water at all.

 

NOTE

 

• Oxygen (Option 2): Not the gas evolved in this reaction; oxygen from water combines with iron to form iron oxide, it is not released as free gas.

 

• Ammonia (Option 3): Not related to the iron-water/steam reaction; ammonia (NH₃) is produced via processes like the Haber process involving nitrogen and hydrogen.

 

• Methane (Option 4): Not related to the iron-water/steam reaction; methane (CH₄) is a hydrocarbon, unrelated to this metal-steam reaction.
